target.title: Recognize Ollama WorkOS session cookies
target.body:
## Summary
- add the WorkOS AuthKit `wos-session` cookie to the Ollama session-cookie allowlist
- recognize `wos-session` in both the manual cookie-header resolver and the imported-browser-cookie selector
- keep legacy Ollama / NextAuth / `__Secure-session` cookie names working

## Live runtime proof

A live probe linked against `CodexBarCore` drove the real `OllamaUsageFetcher` against `https://ollama.com/settings` with a synthetic (invalid) `wos-session` cookie and a redirect logger. No real account or secret was used:

```text
$ swift test --disable-sandbox --filter LiveOllamaWorkOSProbe
resolveManualCookieHeader accepted wos-session: true
resolved header: wos-session=probe-invalid-session; theme=dark
selectSessionInfo accepted wos-session-only: true
[ollama] Using manual cookie header
[ollama] Cookie names: wos-session, theme
[ollama] Redirect 303 https://ollama.com/settings -> https://ollama.com/signin
[ollama] Redirect 303 https://ollama.com/signin -> https://api.workos.com/user_management/authorize?client_id=...&provider=authkit&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code
[ollama] Redirect 302 https://api.workos.com/user_management/authorize?... -> https://signin.ollama.com/?client_id=...&authorization_session_id=01KWWXY00VJ6BR3RW21VXK03C3
[ollama] Response: 200 https://signin.ollama.com/?client_id=...
[ollama] Parse failed: Could not parse Ollama usage: Missing Ollama usage data.
RESULT: fetch threw -> parseFailed("Missing Ollama usage data.")
✔ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed after 1.755 seconds.
```

On `main`, the same probe throws `noSessionCookie` from `resolveManualCookieHeader` and the imported-cookie selector rejects a `wos-session`-only session, because the allowlist omits that name. With this branch, `wos-session` is recognized in both the manual-header path and the browser-import selector, and the real fetcher sends it against `ollama.com` (the captured redirect chain above is the live Ollama/WorkOS sign-in flow).

The cookie is synthetic and invalid, so the live endpoint (correctly) does not authenticate; the proof target is cookie-name recognition and the real fetch path, not a successful usage read.

## Note for the maintainer
The real Ollama WorkOS sign-in flow (captured live above) uses `api.workos.com/user_management/authorize` as an intermediate hop and lands on `signin.ollama.com`. The `wos-session` cookie is the session name WorkOS AuthKit issues after a successful sign-in; recognizing it lets CodexBar import a real WorkOS-authenticated browser session instead of only legacy NextAuth/Ollama session names. No live authenticated account was available to capture a successful usage read, so the success path remains covered by the focused injected-transport tests (the selector and resolver accept `wos-session`; existing tests cover the parse path).

## Testing
- `swift test --disable-sandbox --filter OllamaUsageFetcherTests` (21 passed, incl. new `manual mode accepts workos session cookie header` and `cookie selector accepts workos session cookie`)
- live probe above against the real `ollama.com` / WorkOS sign-in flow (1.76s)
- `swift build` clean
